title: Cohomology over an open commutes with a derived inverse limit
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $D(\mathcal O_X)$ be the derived category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $(K_n,f_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. For an open subset $U\subseteq X$ let $R\Gamma(U,-):D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ be the right derived functor of the sections functor $\Gamma(U,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$, computed by K-injective resolutions: $R\Gamma(U,K)$ is represented by $\Gamma(U,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ for any K-injective resolution $K\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist, def-pur-kinjective-complex], and put $H^m(U,K)=H^m(R\Gamma(U,K))$. Let $(K,p,\delta)$ be a derived limit of the system [def-weil-derived-limit], written $K=R\varprojlim_nK_n$ (any one; derived limits exist but are not unique up to canonical isomorphism), with Roos triangle $K\xrightarrow{p}\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{\delta}K[1]$ and projections $\mathrm{pr}_n:\prod_nK_n\to K_n$. Then: (1) $R\Gamma(U,-)$ commutes with the derived limit: $R\Gamma(U,K)$ is a derived limit of the system $(R\Gamma(U,K_n),R\Gamma(U,f_n))$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, the image under $R\Gamma(U,-)$ of the Roos triangle of $K$, with $R\Gamma(U,\prod_nK_n)$ identified with $\prod_nR\Gamma(U,K_n)$ through the maps $R\Gamma(U,\mathrm{pr}_n)$, being a Roos triangle of that system; that is, $R\Gamma(U,R\varprojlim_nK_n)=R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(U,K_n)$ in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. (2) For every integer $m$ there is a short exact sequence $$0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{m-1}(U,K_n)\to H^m(U,R\varprojlim_n K_n)\to\varprojlim_n H^m(U,K_n)\to0,$$ whose right map is $\gamma\mapsto\bigl(H^m(U,\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p)(\gamma)\bigr)_n$; here $\varprojlim_n$ and $R^1\varprojlim_n$ are taken for the inverse systems of abelian groups with transition maps $H^q(U,f_n)$.

proof.text: The site of open subsets of $X$ is small and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings, so $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian and every complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules has a K-injective resolution [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist, def-pur-kinjective-complex]; the same holds for $\operatorname{Ab}$, the modules over the constant ring $\mathbf Z$ on the one-point space. The functor $\Gamma(U,-)$ is additive, and it carries every small limit in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, in particular every product, to the corresponding limit of abelian groups, because limits of module sheaves are computed sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise]. By [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], $R\Gamma(U,-):D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ commutes with shifts and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. Both $D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $D(\operatorname{Ab})$ have countable products, by [lem-pc-ringed-space-derived-products] and by part (2) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] together with the exactness of products in $\operatorname{Ab}$ [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products]; in particular a derived limit $K$ as in the statement exists by part (1) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence].

$R\Gamma(U,-)$ preserves the product of every tower. Choose K-injective resolutions $K_n\to\mathcal I_n^\bullet$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The termwise product $\prod_n\mathcal I_n^\bullet$ is K-injective and, with its termwise projections, represents $\prod_nK_n$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective]. Hence $R\Gamma(U,\prod_nK_n)$ is represented by $\Gamma(U,\prod_n\mathcal I_n^\bullet)$, which by Step 1 is the termwise product $\prod_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal I_n^\bullet)$ with the projections $\Gamma(U,\mathrm{pr}_n)$; by part (2) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (products in $\operatorname{Ab}$ being exact [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products]) this termwise product represents $\prod_nR\Gamma(U,K_n)$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. So the maps $R\Gamma(U,\mathrm{pr}_n)$ exhibit $R\Gamma(U,\prod_nK_n)$ as the product of the $R\Gamma(U,K_n)$. By Step 1 the functor $R\Gamma(U,-)$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-pc-homotopy-limit-map], which therefore sends the Roos triangle of $K$ to a homotopy-limit (Roos) cone of the tower $(R\Gamma(U,K_n))$: under the identification just made, $R\Gamma(U,1-s)$ is the transition endomorphism $1-s$ of the image tower (Stacks Tag 08U1; the same argument as the node lem-pc-derived-functor-commutes-derived-limit, which is not cited because its statement assumes $X$ a scheme). Thus $(R\Gamma(U,K),R\Gamma(U,p),R\Gamma(U,\delta))$, after the identification, is a derived limit of $(R\Gamma(U,K_n))$ [def-weil-derived-limit], which is part (1).

proof.text: Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the Roos triangle of $(R\Gamma(U,K_n))$ from Step 2. By part (2) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] and the exactness of products in $\operatorname{Ab}$ [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products], $H^q(\prod_nR\Gamma(U,K_n))=\prod_nH^q(U,K_n)$ through the maps $H^q(\mathrm{pr}_n)$ (cohomology of a termwise product of complexes of abelian groups is the product of the cohomologies, via the projections), and under this identification $H^q(1-s)$ is the map $1-s$ of the inverse system $(H^q(U,K_n),H^q(U,f_n))$, since $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ(1-s)=\mathrm{pr}_n-f_n\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$ [def-weil-derived-limit]. The long exact sequence thus contains the exact segment $\prod_nH^{m-1}(U,K_n)\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nH^{m-1}(U,K_n)\to H^m(U,K)\to\prod_nH^m(U,K_n)\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nH^m(U,K_n)$, whose middle-right map is $\gamma\mapsto(H^m(U,\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p)(\gamma))_n$. By [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups], $\ker(1-s)=\varprojlim_nH^m(U,K_n)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(1-s)\cong R^1\varprojlim_nH^{m-1}(U,K_n)$, which gives the short exact sequence of part (2) with the stated right map. (This is the sequence of [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] for the tower $(R\Gamma(U,K_n))$, with its maps named.)
